rationale.text: The test applies only to decorative images without a caption, and code cannot tell which images those are. The glossary defines a decorative image as one with no function and no particular information relative to the content it goes with, and the caption glossary adds that an image whose adjacent text can stand in for it may be treated as decorative. Whether an image has a caption is partly judgment too: the caption glossary covers adjacent text that informs on the image, not only figure and figcaption. So no check can fault an element as surely in scope, nor pass a page, and the entry stays at none, although each condition of the test is mechanical once an element is known to be in scope. The wording says "ces conditions", and the methodology checks them together before "le test est validé", so each condition is its own requirement with one route. The caption limit is an exception on each, from the wording and technical note 1. Technical note 2 extends the conditions to an <svg> displayed through a <use href> child, so each requirement says so. Whether a <text> child is a text alternative or decorative lettering, which the glossary leaves open, is judgment as well. No axe rule is tagged. The custom check custom/1-2-svg-hidden-title-desc reports an <svg> that has aria-hidden="true", the author's sign of a decorative image, and still contains a <title> or <desc> with text. It examines only the condition on <title> and <desc>, so it is linked to that requirement alone, through its single route; it does not examine the caption exception. Its scope is partial: it looks only at svg elements that already have aria-hidden="true", and does not follow <use> references. Its fault is evidence only, because an svg hidden with aria-hidden may be informative (wrongly hidden, a failure of another criterion) or captioned. Applicability is judgment. Needs is empty.
